subject: Science
topicName: Chemistry - Lesson 8: Conservation of Mass: Why Equations Must Balance
description: Explain the Law of Conservation of Mass, use simple mass-in equals mass-out calculations, and check whether chemical equations have equal atom counts on both sides.
learningObjectives: State the Law of Conservation of Mass in your own words
Explain that atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, during chemical reactions
Use conservation of mass to solve simple reactant-product mass problems
Count atoms of each element on both sides of a chemical equation
Explain why balanced equations must have equal atom counts on both sides
Distinguish between changing coefficients and changing subscripts when balancing equations
prerequisites: Identifying reactants and products in a chemical equation
Reading chemical formulas with element symbols and subscripts
Understanding coefficients as numbers placed before formulas
Basic addition of whole-number masses in grams
Recognizing that chemical reactions rearrange atoms into new substances
